title: test(plugin-view): take the render out of ObjectView's contractEnvelope waitFor predicates
body:
Fixes #7802

Both `ObjectView` `contractEnvelope` pins called `deliveredThrough` — which
renders — from inside a `waitFor` predicate. Neither blew up, and that is the
whole card: they were bounded by an RTL implementation detail, not by a
contract. This takes the render out of both predicates. Only the two test files
and a changeset change; `ObjectView.tsx` is untouched, and no case is deleted,
skipped or weakened.

All readings below were taken at `558084dee`.

## The shared helper: no callers outside these two files

⚠️ The card describes `deliveredThrough` as "shared by both files". It is not
one module: **each file declares its own private copy** (`6726:75`,
`6840:104`), neither is exported, and `git grep deliveredThrough` over the repo
returns **8 lines, all inside these two files** — 2 declarations and 6 call
sites. So changing it reaches nothing outside this card's surface, and no
duplicate helper was introduced to avoid the question.

## The mechanism, measured on THIS helper

Five arms with `interval` pinned **AT** `timeout` (2000/2000) unless stated, so
the interval timer can never re-run the predicate and every run past the first
is MutationObserver-driven. Cap: settle at 200 runs.

| predicate | runs | ms | timed out | `document.body` growth |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|--:|
| sync, renders into the document | **200** | **191** | no | **200** |
| sync, renders into a **detached** container | 1 | 2006 | yes | 0 |
| inert | 1 | 2002 | yes | 0 |
| **`async` — the shape these two files had** | **1** | **2003** | yes | **1** |
| the same `async` shape at the default **50 ms** interval | **19** | 2006 | yes | **19** |

200 runs where the interval permitted exactly one is objectui#7756's
worker-killing shape. The `async` shape is **not** self-feeding — 1 run pinned,
19 at the plain 50 ms cadence — because `wait-for.js`'s `checkCallback`
early-returns while `promiseStatus === 'pending'`, so a DOM mutation cannot
re-enter a predicate still in flight. It still **leaks one node per run**
(growth equals the run count exactly, both rows): RTL's `unmount()` tears down
the React root but leaves the container div `render` appended to
`document.body`. Bounded by the timeout — bounded by an accident.

## The lit control: the accidental barrier is real, and it is all that was holding

⭐ `6726:103`'s predicate mutated from `async` to **synchronous**, everything
else unchanged — the exact "simplification" the card warns about:

```diff
-await waitFor(async () => expect(await deliveredThrough(asData)).toHaveLength(2));
+await waitFor(() => expect(deliveredThrough(asData)).toHaveLength(2));
```

Proved on disk before each run: bare-anchor count 1 to 0, mutated-anchor count
0 to 1, blob hash `46d4e6401...` to `c0527a102...`.

| run | heap ceiling | outcome |
|:--|:--|:--|
| default pool (threads) | 4096 MB | **no test output at all**; killed at the 480 s wall (`exit 124`) |
| `--pool=forks` | 4096 MB | **no test output at all**; killed at the 480 s wall (`exit 124`) |
| `--pool=forks` | **512 MB** | **heap exhausted, worker dead**, `exit 1`, in 26.84 s |

Reported honestly: at the 4096 MB ceiling neither pool reached the allocation
limit inside a 480 s wall — both were killed by `timeout` with only the `RUN`
banner in the log, so **neither carries V8 frames or a `tests` line and neither
is quoted for them**. Lowering the ceiling to 512 MB reaches the same unbounded
allocation quickly, and `--pool=forks` is what captures it — under the default
pool the reporter dies with the worker (measured on objectui#7756):

```
FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
 7: v8::internal::HeapAllocator::AllocateRawWithRetryOrFailSlowPath(...)
 9: v8::internal::Runtime_AllocateInYoungGeneration(...)
Error: [vitest-pool]: Worker forks emitted error.
Caused by: Error: Worker exited unexpectedly
 Test Files   (1)
      Tests   (3)
     Errors  1 error
   Duration  26.84s (transform 4.89s, setup 372ms, import 9.17s, tests 0ms, ...)
```

`tests 0ms` — nothing was ever reported; the shard dies, not one test. The same
file unmutated passes in **508 ms** of `tests` time.

Both mutations were restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` under
`trap ... EXIT INT TERM`, and each restoration is proved **by state**, not by
whether the trap fired: blob hash back to `46d4e6401...` **and**
`git diff HEAD` for that path empty (0 bytes). 2 of 2.

## A second reading the card did not ask for, and the repair needs

Removing the outer `waitFor` also removes a **retry** that was papering over an
imprecise readiness signal, so that signal had to be checked rather than
assumed. It does not hold: `ObjectView` starts its rows state at an empty array and
hands the child `data={[]}` **three times** before the fetch lands — measured
delivery sequence for `asData`: `[0, 0, 0, 2]`. So
`await waitFor(() => expect(delivered.length).toBeGreaterThan(0))` is satisfied
by an **empty** delivery, and the helper only returned the right rows because
RTL's act-flush happened to have processed `setData` first.

Deferring `find()`'s answer shows it, 2 envelopes x 4 deferrals x 2 readiness
variants — `rows` returned vs wanted:

| deferral | `asData` (want 2) | `asRecords` (want 0) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 0 ms | plain **2** · settled **2** | plain 0 · settled 0 |
| 50 ms | plain **0 FAIL** · settled **2** | plain 0 · settled 0 |
| 200 ms | plain **0 FAIL** · settled **2** | plain 0 · settled 0 |
| 500 ms | plain **0 FAIL** · settled **2** | plain 0 · settled 0 |

⚠️ The `asRecords` column is the sharper half: "plain" passes there at every
deferral, but **vacuously** — it reads the initial empty delivery before the
answer exists, so the refusal pin would stay green even if the component *did*
read `records`. So the helper now waits on `find()`'s own settled answer first:

```js
await waitFor(() => expect(ds.find).toHaveBeenCalled());
await ds.find.mock.results[0].value;   // a pure read of the mock's call record
await waitFor(() => expect(delivered.length).toBeGreaterThan(0));
```

That is a pure read — no DOM is touched — and it makes all eight cells above
read the answer instead of the mount's initial state.

## The repair, and the acceptance reading

Both cases now assert on the helper's answer directly, which is the shape the
other two cases in each file already had:

```diff
-await waitFor(async () => expect(await deliveredThrough(asData)).toHaveLength(2));
+expect(await deliveredThrough(asData)).toHaveLength(2);
```

⭐ Acceptance property — **the predicate no longer mutates the DOM** — measured
two ways:

1. **Instrumented**: 50 consecutive runs of the repaired helper made **150
   `waitFor` predicate invocations** with `document.body` growth **inside those
   predicates == 0**, and all 50 returned the two rows.
2. **Mechanical**: a repo-wide scan (**2571** test files, brace-balanced,
   following same-file helpers transitively) for `render(` reachable from inside
   a `waitFor` predicate reports **2 hits, both in
   `plugin-detail/RelatedList.lookupLabelResolution.test.tsx`** — objectui#7756's
   file, whose fix is PR #7801 and is not merged yet. **Both `plugin-view` files
   are clear.** The same scan before this change reported those two plus these
   two.

⛔ The `async` was **not** dropped anywhere it still guards a rendering
predicate; the helper stays `async` and is simply no longer called from inside
one.

## Green readings at `558084dee`

Exit codes captured before any pipe.

- `vitest run` both files — `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 6 passed (6)`,
  `tests 508ms`, exit 0
- `vitest run packages/plugin-view/` — `Test Files 34 passed (34)`,
  `Tests 297 passed (297)`, exit 0
- `turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/plugin-view` — `16 successful, 16
  total`, exit 0. Through turbo, not a bare `tsc`. **Measured, not assumed**:
  `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` confirms both edited files are program
  inputs (1 hit each).
- `turbo run lint --filter @object-ui/plugin-view` — `2 successful, 2 total`,
  exit 0; **48 files, 0 errors, 308 warnings**, of which the two edited files
  contribute 3 each, all `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` in the style the
  files already used — the `any` count is **unchanged** in both (4 before, 4
  after), so no warning was added.
- `check:control-bytes` — OK (6357 tracked text files scanned)
- `check:vi-mock-specifiers` — OK · `check:vi-mock-inherit` — OK (129 call sites
  on `@object-ui/react` judged, 129 inherit, 0 auto-mocked)
- `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — `✅  No changeset declares a major bump.`

**Declared narrowing**: lint ran 2 of the workspace lint tasks. `eslint.config.js`
declares no type-aware parser options (0 occurrences of `projectService` /
`parserOptions` / `project:`) and each package lints its own directory, so a
change confined to two test files in `plugin-view` cannot move an untouched
package's verdict. CI runs the full farm regardless.

## Changeset gate

`node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, verbatim, exit 0:

```
Compared the working tree with 9ae1e9d95 (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed, 2 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a manifest whose published contract moved, 0 under a package changesets ignores, 1 changeset(s) added.
✅  2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s): .changeset/eighty-pandas-listen.md.
    Every one of them has an EMPTY frontmatter — declared as releasing nothing, which
    is the explicit exemption and a complete answer to this gate.
```

Empty frontmatter, the gate's own exemption: this is test-only, nothing
published moves.

## Fence

`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` is untouched — no defect was found in
it. `packages/plugin-detail/` is untouched: it is objectui#7756's surface and PR
#7801 is in flight there. Clause-② void condition (any non-test file under
`packages/*/src`) was not reached: the diff is 2 test files plus
`.changeset/eighty-pandas-listen.md`.
